description.narrative:
Summary: The most significant, expected project-level impact is derived from the increase in access to finance to women, both workers and retirees. Beyond the project, the main source of expected market impact is derived from expanding the Cajas de Compensacion funding sources, promoting integration in the Chilean economy.
Project Outcome - Stakeholder effects: Increased access to loans for women including women in the low to middle-income segments and retirees: IFC anticipates that the Project will improve access to finance for women, including those who are from the low to middle income segments, and retirees. Los Heroes has over 1.2 mm members and primarily focuses on serving the underserved segments; over 50% of borrowers are women, about 60% of loans are granted to retirees, 80% of loans are granted to borrowers from the low-middle income segments. Market Creation - Integration: Limitations to the sustainable expansion of the Cajas system include limited access to funding sources. The Cajas were solely reliant on domestic funding until 2017, when through a joint cooperation between Los Heroes and IFC, a regulatory change was approved to allow the Cajas to receive funding from international investors. As noted previously, the primary clientele of the Cajas in Chile are the financially underserved and through their reach and market knowledge, essential to address inequality in access to finance. For example, on average, about 78% of Los Heroes loans are granted to affiliated members earning an income that is below the poverty line. Unlocking the funding side bottleneck is, therefore, necessary step to expand access to credit throughout the socio-economic segments in the Country.

The proposed investment (The Project) consists of a 5-year loan of up to US$60 million to Caja de Compensacion de Asignacion Familiar Los Heroes (Caja Los Heroes, Los Heroes or the Company) to expand the Companys women social credit portfolio, consisting of retirees and low-income workers. The financial package comprises an up to US$35 million A loan, out of which US$30 million will be processed in local currency (CLP) and the remaining US$5 million in USD, and an up to US$25 million B Loan which will be fully processed in USD.
